findings.claim: The declared import owner is now named (`ops.conductor.tools.lane_refs.acquire`) and the adapter/coordinator naming conflict is gone, but the documents bind that dotted target only to fixtures ("a fixture imports that symbol from the trusted runtime artifact with its root on the import path") and never declare how the production entry reaches the same module. The only production invocation the documents declare is `python3 -B ops/conductor/tools/lane_mcp.py --config FILE query TOOL [JSON]` (discovery-lever.md:779, lane-mcp-lever.md:52), under which sys.path[0] is ops/conductor/tools, not the artifact root; there is no tracked `ops/__init__.py`, `ops/conductor/__init__.py` or `ops/conductor/tools/__init__.py` (git ls-files shows only three unrelated __init__.py files), so the dotted name resolves only as a PEP 420 namespace package with the artifact root on the import path. An independent test producer, forbidden by the same handoff from reading implementation, therefore cannot tell whether the module object it imports as `ops.conductor.tools.lane_refs` is the one the executed entry loads. This matters beyond naming because D-A47's clean neighbours (A/A, B/B) and the `binding-unverified` / "no discovery module may subsequently reload from mutable paths" rules are stated about the loaded module, so a fixture loading the file under a second module identity witnesses a loading regime the declared entry does not use. Bounded declaration gap, one sentence to close; it undoes none of the five preserved resolutions and none of the six dispositions.
